item.title: 约翰·雷吉扎莫是一位高贵的研究员
item.description:
2026-07-27T10:00:00.000Z

现在，由于克里斯托弗·诺兰的大片，观众们对奥德赛产生了狂热，观众们正在重新审视他们在英语课上第一次遇到的角色：狡猾的战士、酷酷的怪物、岛上的妖精。不过，说实话。您还记得奥德修斯忠实的猪倌尤迈厄斯（Eumaeus），他在伊萨卡等待主人归来吗？约翰·雷吉扎莫也没有这么做，诺兰不久前带他去 Odeon 餐厅吃午饭，并邀请他出演这个角色。 “我试图不吃东西，因为我吐了很多，”雷吉扎莫最近回忆道。 “他说，‘你将扮演西方文学中最忠诚的角色。’我当时就想，哇，这可是大事啊！”

雷吉扎莫在波哥大和皇后区长大，他在警察广场一号附近的默里伯格特劳姆高中读过《奥德赛》。 “我并没有真正注意，”他在列克星敦大道上的一家地中海餐厅说道。他穿着一件紧身黑色T恤，脖子上挂着链子，用餐巾捂住嘴唇，以免喷出水。 “我只是想出去玩——和女孩们一起出去玩，参加派对，搞笑什么的。”十九岁时，他利用自己的时间重读了这部史诗。 “我试图拯救自己，因为我已经在肯德基工作了两年，”他继续说道。九十年代，他因表演《Mambo Mouth》和《Spic-O-Rama》等顽皮的独角戏而名声大噪，像《奥德赛》中的古代歌手一样，将自己置于口头传统之中。

最近，雷吉扎莫一直在阅读丹尼尔·门德尔松（Daniel Mendelsohn）翻译的荷马史诗，其中将尤迈乌斯描述为“高贵的家伙”。诺兰对这个角色有自己的看法。他给六十六岁、精神抖擞的雷吉扎莫化上了老人妆，戴上了白内障遮盖的隐形眼镜，还把他的头发漂白成了白色。 “第一次的时候我的眉毛被烧伤了，”雷吉扎莫说。他在片场的大部分时间都浑身脏兮兮的。 “我感觉非常难看，”他回忆道。 “我当时想，哦，天哪，每个人看起来都棒极了！马特·达蒙看起来棒极了。汤姆·赫兰德看起来帅极了。我看起来就像一匹骟马，你知道吗。”他的许多场景都是在西西里岛悬崖边的城堡里拍摄的，与猪、驴和牛（必须用直升机运送上山）以及葡萄牙波登戈一起表演，这些葡萄牙波登戈分别扮演奥德修斯的猎犬阿古斯的角色。 “这是一个古老的品种，”他说。 “我称它为葡萄牙语Pendejo ，因为它不是世界上最聪明的狗。Pendejo 在西班牙语中的意思是“笨蛋”。 ”

午餐后，雷吉扎莫步行前往位于六十街的希森堡古代艺术画廊。店主兰德尔·希森博 (Randall Hixenbaugh) 在一个摆满半身像、罐子和头盔的房间里迎接了他。雷吉扎莫曾担心希森鲍是盗墓者，但穿着牛津衬衫和卡其裤的商人向他保证，这些文物——来自希腊、罗马、埃及和美索不达米亚——来自先前的收藏。希森鲍打开一个展示柜，拿出一个青铜时代晚期（大约是奥德修斯时代）的陶瓷花瓶。 “这就是所谓的马镫容器，”他解释道。 “这可能是为了给葡萄酒调味。”

他试图把它交给雷吉扎莫。 “哦，不，我太害怕了，”演员退缩着说道。

“我认为，这就是收集古代艺术品的乐趣所在——它并不都是神圣不可侵犯的，”希森博说。他找到了一个产于公元前 460 年左右的雅典双耳细颈瓶，上面画着一名身穿束腰外衣的士兵离家出走的图案。

“现在，为什么这个人赤身裸体，而另一个人却没有？”雷吉扎莫指着另一个双耳瓶问道。 “他是神吗？”

“是的，这就是狄俄尼索斯，”希森鲍说。 “真正重要的人物也经常赤身裸体，比如亚历山大大帝。”

附近有一个罗马奥德修斯雕像，来自公元一世纪，雷吉扎莫的眼睛在七万五千美元的价格标签上凸出。 “这几乎是我拍电影的全部片酬了！”他说。 “如果更便宜的话，我会把它给马特。”

后面是一堵古希腊盔甲墙，包括头盔、盾牌和护踝（以保护跟腱）。他们看到了一件公元前四世纪的青铜胸甲，上面有肚脐和漂亮的乳头。 “这会吓坏对手，”希森鲍说。 “想象一下，如果希腊人正在与一些没有盔甲的野蛮人作战，而这个家伙看起来就像是用金属制成的。”

“机器人！”雷吉扎莫说道。

希森鲍解释说，青铜时代的希腊人的地理范围有限。 “《奥德赛》就是这样。奥德修斯正在探索青铜时代希腊世界的边界，这非常神秘。他们并不知道地平线上有什么。”

“我要告诉克里斯·诺兰，他应该和你谈谈，”雷吉扎莫说。他预测这部电影将为希森博带来顾客。纽约首映当晚，雷吉扎莫给诺兰找到了一份礼物：一枚银币，来自爱琴海的萨索斯岛，大约于公元前 140-110 年铸造，上面刻有戴奥尼索斯的花环头像，价格合理，为 750 美元。 “你带信用卡吗？”他问道。 ❖

item.title: 约翰尼·诺克斯维尔，美国恶作剧之神
item.description:
2026-07-27T10:00:00.000Z

约翰尼·诺克斯维尔没有记录他骨折了多少根骨头。今年夏天早些时候，当被问及要电话号码时，他犹豫了。 《蠢驴》系列的明星兼联合创始人诺克斯维尔认为，会计概念很愚蠢。 “两位数，”停顿了很长时间后他告诉我。 “我的脚踝各三次。手臂。手。肘部。很多。”

这是一个承重单元，“很多”。诺克斯维尔的其他工伤包括尿道撕裂、眼眶骨折导致眼球脱位（通俗地说，就是眼球部分突出）、椎间盘突出、割伤、烧伤和十六次脑震荡。只有两名原版《蠢驴》演员仍然拥有自己的牙齿，而诺克斯维尔不是其中之一。

三个电视季、五部电影和众多衍生剧共同构成了全球“傻瓜”的霸主，其格式都很简洁。其中，男人（后来还有一名女人）表演特技和恶作剧。其中一些片段是提升到三维空间的单行：一个人向喇叭放屁，一个人撑竿跳入棕榈树。有些人奇特地使用捕鼠器、桶、炸药、弹弓、高跷、厕所、走钢丝和其他经典喜剧道具。其中有令人作呕的笑点（“运动装鸡尾酒”、“屁股穿孔”）和大量的阴茎动作。有些特技以数学般的优雅表达了肢体喜剧的通用语言：一个穿着尼龙搭扣套装的男子在坡道上滑板，撞到了一辆同样涂有尼龙搭扣的过往卡车的侧面，而在卡车旁边，该男子被传送到银幕外。纳博科夫将幽默定义为“失去平衡——以及对失去平衡的欣赏”，概括了《傻瓜》的精神和机制。

如果没有可爱的演员阵容，《蠢驴》就不可能成功，但诺克斯维尔显然是罪魁祸首。当你看到他撞上水果车或电死他的朋友时，你很容易把他想象成一个从奥林匹斯山派下来供高等实体娱乐的小神——一个对那些无力抵抗或理解他的凡人发出恶作剧的使者。 “把这个装满，”你想象宙斯在诺克斯维尔摩托艇穿过花园树篱时说道。

这位明星以他的笑声而闻名，听起来就像友军开火一样，而且他的脸非常英俊。但最重要的是，他以比任何同龄人更频繁、更快乐地冒着生命危险而闻名。为了拍摄这段视频，诺克斯维尔穿着溜冰鞋被一群水牛冲锋，被多头公牛攻击，被牦牛翻身，被大炮射中，绑在火箭上，并被一名重量级拳击手击倒。 《Jackass》不仅激发了模仿电视节目和 YouTube 明星的灵感——先生。 Beast、Paul 兄弟——还有互联网的所有类别，包括 DIY 恶作剧内容、挑战视频和失败汇编。

在一小群专业人士——足球运动员、特技演员、综合格斗选手——为了大众娱乐而花钱毁掉自己的身体的人中，五十五岁的诺克斯维尔被证明是极其耐用的。第五部、据称是最后一部电影《蠢蛋：最佳与最后》的拍摄于二月杀青，距该系列首映已有二十六年。这让诺克斯维尔在埃维尔·克尼维尔身上度过了坚实的十年，并且比普通职业拳击手有更多的时间。

过去几年，他在山谷里租了一套房子。他的社区有一种郊区的自我控制感，房屋蹲在整洁的院子后面，院子里种满了抗旱植物。没有一览无遗的景色，也没有建筑上的胜利。在这个街区，你更愿意将其与一位富有的牙医联系在一起，而不是与一位电影明星联系在一起。在一个阳光明媚的工作日，诺克斯维尔穿着泡泡糖粉色短裤从家中出来，一头银色的头发，脸上涂着防晒霜。我们计划去冲浪。

本季的第一波南涌浪已经到来，很快就会在南加州海岸掀起八英尺高的巨浪。诺克斯维尔并不是一位经验丰富的冲浪者，但他对天气预报并没有感到惊讶。他坐进一辆雪佛兰塔霍汽车的驾驶座，戴上一副太阳镜。 “让我们犯一些错误吧，”他说着，退出了。

他向西行进，翻越了马里布起伏的绿色山丘。当我们向太平洋下降时，空气和地形变得咸味。停车场爆满。季节性海浪的第一天总是一件疯狂的事情，我们看到冲浪者冲向大海，就像在近海发现了金子一样。诺克斯维尔 (Knoxville) 停泊的杜姆角 (Point Dume) 是一片飞地，在 20 世纪 90 年代仍保留着一些海滨风情。现在这里是卡马拉·哈里斯和谢尔盖·布林拥有房屋的地方。

“我像一只残废的大猩猩一样冲浪，”诺克斯维尔在沙滩上警告我，同时穿上厚厚的潜水衣。我们看到一名冲浪者跳入海浪中，划出专业的线条，拍打嘴唇，将喷射的水花喷射到他朋友的脸上。 （希望是他的朋友。）诺克斯维尔爬上冲浪板，划桨出去，中途停下来解开皮带上的一条海藻丝带。到达队列后，他坐直了身子。 “我没想到我能成功！”他说。

诺克斯维尔一边休息一边对天气和砂岩悬崖的景色表示赞赏。他似乎很高兴在阳光下，很高兴在水中，很高兴穿着潜水衣撒尿。有时，他会走神，凝视远方，不再说话。 “抱歉，”他在一次出神后说道。 “有时我会去蒂华纳呆一会儿。”

当一盘到来时，诺克斯维尔毫不犹豫地瞄准了巨大的波浪。他以风车般的速度从我们在岸边仰慕的冲浪者身边驶过，后者因害怕遭到屠杀而后退。波浪起伏。诺克斯维尔突然出现，飞向海滩一百码，就像孩子在滑索上一样轻松。旅程结束时，他下马，转身，被更猛烈的海浪拍打。他的冲浪板飞向天空，消失在泡沫漩涡中。他的银色头颅在一次翻滚中丢失了。当海浪向浅滩延伸时，一切都安静下来，然后一声叫声打破了寂静。

那些最了解他的人对诺克斯维尔的说法感到困惑——好吧，没有人就如何称呼它达成一致。胆大妄为？愚蠢吗？疯狂？强迫症？损害？勇气？受虐狂？ “我不知道如何准确地描述它，”《蠢驴》每一期的制作人斯派克·琼斯说。 “它不是来自外在。而是一种内在的品质。”诺克斯维尔的表弟罗杰·艾伦·韦德（Roger Alan Wade）比大多数活着的人认识他的时间都长，他同样被难住了：“他有一颗金子般的心和与之匹配的灵魂。最大的谜团是他那狂欢节般的大脑里到底在转来转去。”

诺克斯维尔的无论如何都颠覆了电影制作本身的逻辑。票房好的男主角不会因为表演未经排练的玩命特技而危及自己的生命。 “傻瓜”片场的医务人员被要求尽可能保持克制，以免毁掉好的镜头。 “你应该为好莱坞故事片中的男主角投保，让他完好无损，”演员斯蒂芬·格洛弗（化名史蒂夫-O）说。 “这没有意义。”

在第一次骨折后，诺克斯维尔的家人和朋友对此感到毫无意义，而且他们现在也无法理解这一点。他因特技赢得了名声、财富和评论界的赞誉，但他可能在没有遭受如此多的脑外伤的情况下完成了这些事情。他有三个孩子、一个妻子和一个他深爱的大家庭。没有人强迫他进入斗牛场或用枪指着自己。那么他为什么要这么做呢？是什么让约翰尼跑步？

要寻找线索，最好从他的田纳西州家乡开始，他的艺名就是从那里开始的。诺克斯维尔出生于 1971 年，原名菲利普·约翰·克拉普 (Philip John Clapp)，有着明显的南方血统。他在洛杉矶生活了足够长的时间，已经从句子中去掉了“先生”和“女士”，但敬语仍然隐含在其中。门一直开着，“请”和“谢谢”很快就会送达。他彬彬有礼，效率低下，确保触手可及的每个人都感到舒适、水分充足，并能乘车前往他们下一步要去的任何地方。

诺克斯维尔的父母菲尔·克拉普和莱莫恩·霍克·克拉普就读于诺克斯维尔的竞争对手高中。菲尔是一位明星运动员和火腿。莱莫恩拥有电影明星般的美丽，并且让每个人都知道这一点。这家人住在一栋带双车库的错层房子里。后面有树林，前面有玫瑰丛，院子里有一匹名叫波·迪德利的小马。菲尔经营着一家从父亲那里继承的轮胎公司。莱莫恩负责烤黑底馅饼并料理家务。邻里关系十分紧密。当博·迪德利（Bo Diddley）逃离他的围栏时，整个街区都呈扇形展开追捕他。

诺克斯维尔是家里的宝贝，分别比他的姐姐克里斯登和林恩晚出生七岁和十年。这是一次意外怀孕。婴儿时期的诺克斯维尔非常丰满。吃饭的时候，他吃得很快，以至于需要一群克拉普雌性来给男孩的 Infa Feeder 补充果泥。除了喂波·迪德利之外，诺克斯维尔免于做家务。 “他从不修剪院子，”林恩说。 “我们把他宠坏了。”为了省去弟弟走路的麻烦，女孩们把他从一个地方带到另一个地方。当他受到打屁股的威胁时，他们把他从父母手中藏了起来。 “这就像养了一只宠物猴子，”诺克斯维尔的表弟韦德说。 “他们所需要的只是一台风琴研磨机。”

诺克斯维尔一会走路就惹麻烦了。如果林恩去美容院做头发，诺克斯维尔可能会用水气球瞄准新鲜的头发。如果她有约会对象到家里来，他就会像相扑选手一样扯起内衣，然后穿过书房。这些都没有激怒他的母亲。 “PJ 可以杀死教皇，而我妈妈会说，‘教皇罪有应得，’”林恩告诉我。

从女孩们记事起，诺克斯维尔就因为哮喘而进出医院。莱莫恩密切关注着他的呼吸：当她儿子感到气道变窄时，他就会安静下来。每年有好几次，家人都会在他发病时将他送往医院注射肾上腺素。 “我的天啊！”当被问及这些访问时，诺克斯维尔说道。 “我这段时间吸过很多毒，但从来没有这么匆忙过。”他说，肾上腺素就像“同时吸了八球可卡因”。他非常喜欢它。

比肾上腺素更好的是随之而来的感觉。在晚年，诺克斯维尔读到了空军研究员约翰·斯塔普（John Stapp）进行的一系列实验，他的任务是测试人体从飞机上弹射时能承受多大的力。斯塔普把自己绑在火箭驱动的雪橇上，加速到每小时六百英里以上，然后猛地停了下来。在医院里，他经历了他所谓的“生存欣快感”。奇怪的是，斯塔普并没有将其描述为一种喜悦或解脱的感觉。相反，这让他渴望承担更大的风险。当诺克斯维尔读到斯塔普的故事时，他回想起童年时期的哮喘发作和氧气面罩，以及在恢复呼吸之前将他钉在墙上的肾上腺素注射，以及所有这一切与特技后的冲刺相比。是的，就是这样，他想。生存的欣快感。

对关注的热爱和对肾上腺素的渴望：两种暗示性的成分。将诺克斯维尔的父亲加入到这款啤酒中。 “追溯到菲尔，”韦德说。 “他是一个真正的、真实的、原始的混蛋。”菲尔经营他的轮胎公司，是成功的商业和业余马戏团的合并。他的同事们的名字有“屁股踢罗伯特”、“大乔治”、“棚车”和“超级迪克”。当菲尔没有给这些人喂加了 Ex-Lax 的奶昔，也没有给他们寄假的国税局审计信时，他就会用猫鼬盒子这样的滑稽动作来取乐：他公司的陈列室里安装了一个装置，上面写着“猫鼬：请勿触摸”。 “他在盒子周围放了一根绳子，并说：‘谁都不要靠近。这很危险！’ “克里斯登告诉我。 “这当然只会引起更多关注。”当顾客靠近盒子时，菲尔按下开关，弹出一个弹簧填充的毛绒动物。 “人们会跳出他们的皮肤，”克里斯登说。 “我不知道他脑子里的想法是从哪里来的。”

在家里，菲尔喜欢猛地打开浴室的门，把一杯冰水从淋浴顶部泼到儿子身上。 “那是日常生活中的事情，”林恩说。如果莱莫恩要参加 PTA 会议，菲尔可能会打扮成一个流浪者，走进会议，掐他妻子的屁股。他驾驶飞机并用空弹进行枪战。 “说到纯粹的街头智慧，我从未见过有人能与之媲美，”韦德告诉我。 “如果他将其应用于科学，我们就会生活在火星上。但他将其应用于恶作剧。”今天世界对诺克斯维尔的看法正是田纳西州的一个小角落曾经对菲尔·克拉普的看法。

和每个人的童年一样，有好的场景，也有不好的场景。菲尔是个酒鬼。他大声说话，与莱莫恩打架，吓坏了孩子们。 “我一直感到自己很渺小，被欺负，”诺克斯维尔说。菲尔两次开车送儿子去洛杉矶。第一次很顺利。第二次，菲尔失去了兴趣。当他们到达阿卡迪亚时，诺克斯维尔看着他的父亲倒了一大杯半满伏特加和半满水的杯子。 “他像个小孩子一样用双手抓住它，然后就杀了它，”诺克斯维尔说。 “这让我心碎。他非常需要它。”

菲尔于 2018 年去世。当我第一次联系诺克斯维尔讨论撰写个人资料时，他发了一封电子邮件，里面装满了家庭旧照片：菲尔在婚礼当天西装革履、兴高采烈，菲尔抱着婴儿诺克斯维尔在他的腿上大笑，菲尔和儿子穿着相配的淡蓝色服装。最后一张照片显示菲尔躺在 La-Z-Boy 里，躺在发光的圣诞树小饰品下。诺克斯维尔当时已经二十多岁了，坐在他父亲的腿上。两人都喜气洋洋。 “我和我的老伙计，”他写道。 “我非常爱他并且非常想念他。”

童年的最后一幕。为了在炎热的夏日打发时间，诺克斯维尔和一个朋友发明了一种叫做 Nutball 的游戏。规则很简单。三到五个孩子脱光了内衣，阔腿坐在地板上，围成一圈，互相扔台球。他们可以这样做几个小时。有些孩子放风筝，有些孩子喂鸭子，有些孩子遭受生殖器创伤。 1990 年，当诺克斯维尔搬到洛杉矶时，Nutball 帮派的继任者正处于早期阶段。

如果说《Jackass》的后代数量众多，那么该系列本身就有一个明确的起源：一本名为《Big Brother》的滑板杂志。该杂志的创始人史蒂夫·罗科 (Steve Rocco) 是土生土长的加州人，拥有成功的滑板公司 World Industries。 1992年，罗科聘请了一位年轻的艺术学校毕业生杰夫·特里梅因（Jeff Tremaine）（后来担任《蠢驴》的导演）作为编辑。特里梅因儿时的朋友（也是《Jackass》的制片人）斯派克·琼斯 (Spike Jonze) 提供了照片。该杂志的作者包括 Sean Cliver（另一位制片人）和 Chris Pontius（演员）；其中包括 Jason (Wee Man) Acuña（演员）等滑手和 Steve-O（演员）等疯子。

《Big Brother》被塑造成一个无政府主义的替代品，取代了Thrasher和TransWorld等更成熟的滑板杂志，罗科对这些杂志的认真态度感到遗憾。该杂志位于埃尔塞贡多的办公室是用两块四块的金属板和铁丝网​​拼凑而成的。其他杂志专注于滑冰技巧，而《老大哥》的天才之处在于将自己视为一本“生活方式”杂志，这里必须使用一个不幸的词。

除了滑板照片和采访外，该出版物还包含胸部、麦芽酒评论、墨西哥监狱幸存者的描述，以及如何制造假身份证或制作可卡因等 Pixy Stix 糖粉烟枪或鼻烟管的教程。当特里梅因被告知杂志的标题应该以大号字体打印以获得最大的报摊可见度时，他打电话给印刷商并询问最小的可打印字体。下一期将“老大哥”隐藏在封面左上角的四点 Helvetica 字体中。

该杂志作为地下出版物在卧室和学校食堂中流传——早在马诺圈抬起丑陋的头颅之前，这个男孩圈就已经蓬勃发展。对于该杂志的读者来说，奇迹般的结果是传统的创造性成功公式的结果：聚集原始人才，给他们大量现金，用对手嘲笑他们，并取消监督。早在“类社会关系”一词成为影响心理学的简称之前几十年， “老大哥”员工就像情景喜剧中反复出现的角色一样出现在其页面中。读者们写信延续了多年来持续存在的内部笑话。 《Jackass》演员戴夫·英格兰告诉我，他第一次读到这本杂志时，他想，我希望我认识这些人。

诺克斯维尔在进入“老大哥”轨道之前已经在洛杉矶闲逛了一段时间。高中毕业后，他立即在帕萨迪纳的美国戏剧艺术学院参加了为期八周的表演课程。他当时的舞台经历包括两部学校戏剧。约翰尼奔向西部的原因可能不是对舞台的热爱，而是对眼球的渴望，大量的眼球，他似乎是通过淘汰的过程进入演艺圈的：运动受伤使他不适合大学棒球，耳朵聋使他没有资格成为摇滚明星。 “我知道他不适合住在南诺克斯维尔，”他的妹妹琳恩说。 “但我也知道，如果他不做一些伟大的事情，他就不会得到一分钱。因为他不会工作。”

诺克斯维尔在好莱坞租了一套破旧的公寓，在那里他接受了该地区历史悠久的服务业经济，包括服务员、试镜广告以及存入母亲的支票。还有其他一些零工：酒店服务生、搬运工、少年棒球联盟裁判。一位花商付钱让他打扮成翼手龙，站在冷水峡谷大道上推销业务。诺克斯维尔在四十五分钟后因穿着戏服闯入电话亭而被解雇。

他在一部音乐录影带中认识了特里梅因。尽管诺克斯维尔不会滑冰，但他在“老大哥”身上看到了一群与他志趣相投的冒险家。该杂志中介绍的滑冰类型需要强迫性重复、恶魔般的疼痛阈值以及海盗般的眼睛来识别最适合掠夺的公共和私人财产类型。你不可能为诺克斯维尔未来的帮派设计一个更好的候选人库，为他的演员们设计一个更好的训练营。

但还不止于此。滑冰使人习惯于失败。要想成功，需要进行大量的试验和错误——一个人可能会尝试一百次，但都失败了——而且这通常发生在由同龄人组成的无情陪审团面前。在这种情况下，怎么可能有人不对失败产生一种禅宗般的分寸感呢？这种心态无缝地转化为“傻瓜”，最大的失败引来最大的笑声。

诺克斯维尔向老大哥讲述了一个关于测试自卫装备的故事，包括一罐胡椒喷雾、电击枪、泰瑟枪和防弹背心。测试对象将是作者。 “把它拍下来，”特里梅因告诉诺克斯维尔。由此产生的录像带显示，一名年轻男子在胡椒喷雾喷射后在地上尖叫，被泰瑟枪的力量击倒，在十二万伏电击枪的作用下翻滚。这听起来像是“60 分钟”特别节目中可能出现的片段，讲述了年轻人冒险行为的危机。但银幕上出现的诺克斯维尔——二十七岁，用橡胶和勇气锻造而成，披着美国国旗作为斗篷——证明了魅力可以迷惑任何遇到的人。滑板的另一个对称之处是：“你可以做出最难的动作，但如果它看起来像机器人，没有人愿意看到它，”演员巴姆·马格拉（Bam Margera）告诉我。 “你想让自己看起来没有燃烧卡路里。就像你在世上无忧无虑地漂浮着。黄油般的、轻松的、简单的。”

诺克斯维尔最难的技巧涉及防弹背心，他计划绑上防弹背心，并通过哄骗朋友用 0.38 口径的史密斯威森射击他来测试。枪手在最后一刻退出，不想让自己卷入可能的谋杀案。摄影师也退出了，因为不想让自己卷入一部可能的鼻烟电影中——但在诺克斯维尔说服他将相机支撑在一个表面上并将其调整到正确的方向之前。为了获得额外的保护，他在凯夫拉背心下塞了几本色情杂志——两本《骗子》 ，两本《腿部世界》 ——然后向自己的腹部开枪。录像显示，他向后挺身，避免摔倒，然后跳进一辆逃跑的汽车。他的 T 恤上被火药烧焦了。当特里梅因看到这段视频后，他给斯派克·琼斯打了电话。 “我认为这里有一个电视节目，”他说。

《Jackass》于 2000 年在 MTV 上首次亮相。诺克斯维尔的演员阵容几乎全部来自滑板界，该剧廉价而快速的审美观是从滑板视频中大量引进的。 “像我们这样的人可以拍摄男孩们自古以来所做的事情，” 《老大哥》的编辑戴夫·卡尼说。 “你知道亨利八世小时候就做过‘傻瓜’之类的事。他只是没有摄像机。”卡尼说，可以对这部剧的起源做出一个粗略的物质解释：“我们是拿着新玩具的傻孩子。”

这部剧一炮而红，也迅速成为热点。该剧首映几个月后，康涅狄格州一名十三岁男孩模仿素描自焚。随后至少发生了另外两起模仿事件。参议员乔·利伯曼 (Joe Lieberman) 对媒体的暴力行为感到热泪盈眶，他说服 MTV 取消或改革该节目。该电视台发表声明否认承担责任，但指出“显然，当年轻人做出伤害自己的事情时，我们感到很可怕”，然后又制作了另一季的节目，其中年轻人总是这样做，而且只这样做。

MTV 聘请了一名安全主管来审查特技创意。 “这个人试图将普通工作场所OSHA标准应用于我们想做的任何事情，”制片人肖恩·克莱弗 (Sean Cliver) 说。在“便便尿布”等特技表演中，戴夫·英格兰穿着破烂的衣服，走近一个公共垃圾桶，在周围挖掘，捡起脏尿布，然后吃掉里面的东西。 （尿布里预先装满了巧克力布丁。）MTV 强烈反对“便便尿布”。该剧的巨大成功不可避免地吸引了错误的目光。在诺克斯维尔看来，网络突然对线路的位置（到处）和穿越线路的建议（几乎从不）提出了很多乏味的意见。三个赛季后，他退出了。节目不再好玩，他有了更大的愿望。

《蠢驴大电影》于 2002 年上映，全球票房收入 8000 万美元。第三部电影《Jackass: 3D》使这个数字翻了一番。因为“ OW！ ”在每种语言中都大致相同，所以诸如“Lamborghini Tooth Pull”、“The Bungee Wedgie”、“Anaconda Ball Pit”、“Ass Kicked by Girl”和“Beehive Tetherball”之类的内容在全球范围内无滞后地传播。每个片段的副标题可能是“男孩的欢乐”。比赛的场面令人陶醉。 “玩耍是不可否认的，”荷兰历史学家约翰·惠津加（Johan Huizinga）曾经写道。 “如果你愿意，你可以否认几乎所有抽象概念：正义、美、真理、善良、思想、上帝。你可以否认严肃性，但不能否认游戏。”该团伙继续巡回演出，推出衍生产品，并为一种新颖的女性有机体的诞生感到高兴：“蠢驴”追星族。

男孩当然需要燃料。除了芝士汉堡和啤酒——米勒高级生活赞助了前两部电影——演员们还吞下了堆积如山的毒品。 《蠢驴：电影》由镇痛药（非官方）承保。 “我们喜欢止痛药，”诺克斯维尔说，并补充说，一次与吗啡棒棒糖的艰难遭遇最终让他制定了一条永远不超越维柯丁的规则。成功需要促进剂。 “阿得拉推动了第二部和第三部影片的拍摄，”诺克斯维尔说。 “我们非常专注！”无论如何，我发现大多数演员在医学上似乎都适合服用阿得拉。 “每个人都有一些东西，”诺克斯维尔说。 “如果人们没有东西，你就不会得到这样的镜头。”

《蠢驴》电影并不追求艺术的水平，但它们拥有艺术改变人们看待世界的方式的能力。即使离开剧院仅一个小时，熟悉的风景也会因可能被倾倒、点燃或从楼梯上扔下的物体而闪闪发光。郊区购物中心、城市十字路口、乡村道路：一切都变成了未爆炸的喜剧弹药场。

周四下午，诺克斯维尔计划结束播客采访后直接前往“吉米·坎摩尔现场直播！”为了为黄金时段做好准备，诺克斯维尔在头发上抹了一点润发油，并与制片人通了几分钟电话。不需要其他准备。

尽管诺克斯维尔一路走来成名，但他并没有像许多名人那样需要行政服务——不断地要求提供一瓶水、一个手机充电器、一个电子烟、一杯冰咖啡、提醒现在几点了。他回复短信。他记得生日。如果说诺克斯维尔的“傻瓜”存在具有在头足类动物和火山中比在人类中更常见的爆炸推进力，那么他的私人存在是保留的。他需要证明什么？

播客结束后，诺克斯维尔离开录音室，钻进他的 1970 款凯迪拉克埃尔多拉多，这辆车停在停车场，黑色的内饰吸收着热量。他转动钥匙。凯迪拉克像一只温暖的腿上的猫一样振动。扶手上内置有烟灰缸和安装在控制台上的八轨。

即使在好莱坞，老式凯迪拉克也是一种引人注目的车辆。在前往“金梅尔”的途中，一辆警车粘在了我们的尾巴上。 “我们被跟踪了，”诺克斯维尔说道，然后低声说道，“这是因为我的驾驶方式很奇怪。”巡洋舰在我们旁边缓缓行驶。当警官看到驾驶者是谁时，他打出了和平手势，然后继续前行。衡量名人支持率的一种方法是：执法人员在记录司机的身份后是否更有可能开出罚单。

在停车场，身着黑色西装的“金梅尔”工作人员将诺克斯维尔带到了一条用铁丝网围住的小巷。寻求签名的人们爬过栏杆，在从家里拖来的梯子上摇摇欲坠。 “每次都是同一个人，”一名保安告诉我。 “他们把签名卖给任何人。”

诺克斯维尔很乐意助长这场喧嚣，他在海报上签名，直到制片人出来把他困在里面。

“大楼里有一只浣熊，”制片人告诉他。

“噢，小伙子！”诺克斯维尔说。

关于这只逍遥法外的浣熊的讨论继续进入休息室，边桌上一支带有喜怒无常气味的香薰蜡烛在旁边闪烁。制片人坐下来回顾演出的情况。诺克斯维尔喜欢围绕浣熊做点什么吗？他做到了。如果诺克斯维尔拿着一只假浣熊的尾巴上台，声称抓住了这个混蛋怎么办？伟大的！

诺克斯维尔与金梅尔很友好，并已出现在节目中二十一次。当人们骑车进出休息室时，一位女士承认，尽管认识诺克斯维尔多年，但她仍然不确定该怎么称呼他。是PJ吗？还是约翰尼？或者她应该留在诺克斯维尔？

这是一个广泛存在的不确定性领域。 “我记得在拍摄《永远的傻瓜》的整个过程中，我都不知道该叫他什么，”他的妻子艾米丽·丁 (Emily Ting) 说道。 （丁在最后两部电影中担任服装设计师。）他在电子邮件上签名，有时在短信上签名，比如“探戈先生”或“布丁”或“南诺克斯维尔强男孩”或“亚伯拉罕·林肯·詹金斯”或“爱德华·詹姆斯几乎”，这无济于事。由于名气使诺克斯维尔免于正式介绍的标准仪式，因此在他的圈子里有数量惊人的人选择了逃避。 （“嘿，伙计/朋友/朋友。”）在最近的电影中，Ting 制定了一项政策，在家打电话给她的丈夫 PJ，在工作时给诺克斯维尔打电话。

当录音开始时，每个人都搬到了一个带有酒吧和雅致的仙人掌布置的围栏前。诺克斯维尔喝了一杯威士忌，从监视器上观看。一只假浣熊开着一辆装满核桃的小车在 Kimmel 的舞台上飞驰。

当制片人召唤时，诺克斯维尔向丁提出了最后的服装批准，然后离开了。几秒钟后，他再次出现在监视器上，手里拿着浣熊。 “我抓住了他，”他一边摇晃着道具动物一边告诉基梅尔。 “他没有死。他只是在后台喝了我的威士忌。让他睡一觉吧。”

这一点起作用了。看着诺克斯维尔进入表演模式就像看着一杯静水变成碳酸一样。味道一样，但是有点刺痛。

《金梅尔》杀青后，诺克斯维尔回到凯迪拉克，开车去 In-N-Out 吃零食。他把车驶入免下车通道，引来众人目光——有些人盯着汽车，有些人盯着司机。大多是男性的目光。一个十几岁的男孩走到乘客窗前，倾身接受他的订单。

“一个汉堡加番茄、生菜和芥末，”诺克斯维尔说。 “请给我一份薯条。还有一杯水。”

“洋葱？”

“不，先生。”

少年眯起眼睛。 “你看上去很面熟。你是不是很出名？”

“其实，完全是偶然！” Knoxville improvised.

“Jackass Forever,” which came out in 2022, was meant to be the final installment. Twelve years had passed since the previous film—an eternity in Hollywood, and in the biological lives of stuntmen. Knoxville wasn't sure if audiences would care about the high jinks of middle-aged men. But the film was another hit, grossing eighty million dollars worldwide. Instead of the usual I-can't-believe-they're-doing-that reaction, audiences reacted with I-can't-believe-they're- still -doing-that: a minor but effective update. Midway through filming, Knoxville decided to stop dyeing his hair, which had turned white in his twenties. A visibly wrinkled and graying cast, it turned out, only underlined what “Jackass” had promised all along: that men can be boys at any age.

The film was released in the twilight of the #MeToo movement, when male self-scrutiny was at its most squeamish. As countless books and articles palpated the question of whether it was possible to be an unproblematic man, “Jackass Forever” offered its own (totally unintended) solution to the crisis of masculinity: just don't become a man. Get off the train at the “boy” stop and proceed no further. Cultural expectations of men change at lightning speed, but boys will be boys will be boys. That's one reason the “Jackass” movies have aged well—or, rather, have not aged at all. They belong to the world of “What, me worry?” and “Looney Tunes” and the rampaging ding-dongs of Bruegel's “Children's Games.”

Though the movies reject machismo, they still revel in punishment. Steve-O described the cast as “attention whores battling for screen time. The more terrible the thing that happens to you, the more likely you'll make the cut.” You don't have to be a sociologist to recognize the hazards of this dynamic. If the respect of a person's peers—not to mention his paycheck and access to SAG health insurance—hangs on his willingness to rupture a testicle with a pogo stick, the notion of “consent” wobbles. The jackasses are friends, accomplices, and rivals. Together, they've had fun and made gobs of money and partied their brains out, but they've also harmed each other irreparably.

Among the cast it is tacitly acknowledged that Knoxville is the chief instigator of damage. “Even in the most serious of situations,” Sean Cliver said, “Knoxville can't help himself if he sees an opening.” By “opening,” Cliver meant the opportunity to pitch an object at someone else's nuts. “We're all so PTSD'd from this over the years that we could be standing at a funeral and most everyone would still have one hand cupped over their groin.” Nobody is safe on set. “You gotta keep your wits about you,” Preston Lacy, a cast member, said. “Stay vigilant. Like a fighter pilot.” When I asked Spike Jonze if there was any way to declare oneself off-limits from Knoxville's sprees, he had to stop and think hard about the question. “Not that I'm aware of,” Jonze finally said. “No, I'm pretty sure there's not. It's a little stressful, especially if you're operating a camera.”

Certain people, Cliver said, have had to “distance themselves” from Knoxville, because “when he sets his mind to a prank there really are no bounds to what he can dream up.” In 2024, a segment producer from a non-“Jackass” show brought a lawsuit alleging that Knoxville had nonconsensually chased him down and Tased him, resulting in a number of injuries. (The case has been settled.) “All play is a voluntary activity,” Huizinga, the historian, wrote. It can only be conducted by choice and in freedom. You can't compel someone to play, especially with a conducted-energy weapon.

If Knoxville has a sadistic streak, his cruelest target is always himself. “I have treated a boxer, football players, other athletes,” David Kipper, Knoxville's physician of two decades, told me. “But nothing like him. Knoxville's injuries are not a consequence of his work. In some ways, they are the purpose of his work.” Of his patient's many exotic ailments, it was the urethral tear, in 2008, that stood out to the doctor. The injury occurred during a botched motorcycle stunt. “Now, if you're a guy and you hear the phrase 'self-catheterization,' you start crossing your legs,” he said. Knoxville had to catheterize himself multiple times a day for more than three years. “He was so laissez-faire,” Kipper said. “That was pretty manly of him.” He added, “Amazingly, he was still able to make babies after the injury.”

Because daredevilry is not a sport and has no rules, there is no consensus on what might constitute a career-ending injury. Kipper advised Knoxville to hang up the cape in 2022, when his patient suffered a severe concussion and a brain hemorrhage while filming “Jackass Forever.” In the stunt, Knoxville steps into a bullring with a flourish. The bull charges and hits his target, flipping Knoxville roughly five hundred and forty degrees in the air. Those who were present remember it in snapshots: the crack of skull against hard-packed dirt, the crumple of Knoxville's body, the medics who disregarded their customary order to hover off camera. Knoxville remembers almost nothing.

The months that followed, he said, were a period of “almost sliding off the earth.” Knoxville's mind turned to guacamole. His speech declined; he avoided friends; his second marriage ended. Trips to Tijuana lasted longer than they should have. He took antidepressants for the first time in his life. “Here's a dark reality,” Steve-O said. “My father is eighty-three years old, and every time I speak with him I'm searching for any indication that his cognitive awareness has diminished and that dementia is setting in. It's really dark and messed up that I have those same antennae up in every conversation I have with Knoxville.”

Interviewers occasionally ask Knoxville if he worries about chronic traumatic encephalopathy—or, as the podcaster Dax Shepard put it, “whatever the football thing is.” In these conversations, Knoxville will acknowledge that CTE is an area of concern, and that it cannot yet be diagnosed in a living person. Sometimes he'll crack a little joke about it, saying, “I didn't win any awards for my brain scans.”

Dave Carnie told me that “Jackass” was “best appreciated without giving it too much thought.” Knoxville himself excels at selective underthinking. The bull hit was not his first scrap with the animal that day. In an earlier take, the bull had charged and struck him—but not, in Knoxville's opinion, hard enough for strong footage, so he'd insisted on a second round.一切就这样结束了。 During his six months of recovery, Knoxville found within himself a previously undetected shred of the self-preservation instinct. The days of bulls and rockets and demolition derbies were over.

In May, I attended a test screening of “Jackass: Best and Last” at the Paramount lot. The theatre was stocked with members of the target demo: men aged sixteen to forty. There were baseball hats and hand tattoos, mustaches hesitantly attempted and manfully achieved. There was even a mini altercation: just before showtime, two young men spotted each other across the room, hissed in confrontation, affected to converge, submitted to the calming attempts of bystanders, and took their seats.

Knoxville entered the room as the lights went down. He sat in the center of the fourth row and propped a clipboard on his lap. The screen lit up. “Jackass: Best and Last” mixes new and old footage, and the earlier clips are electrified by Knoxville's cult-leader mania. In the new footage, which was filmed across five days in Santa Clarita, he emits a geniality that can visibly fade into resignation.

In the first ten minutes of the movie, someone offscreen asks Knoxville how he feels. “I'm sad,” he replies.不开玩笑。

There's a Hemingway story, “The Undefeated,” about a veteran bullfighter who can't keep himself out of the ring. Having barely recovered from a nasty injury, the bullfighter begs a promoter to give him a fight. The promoter agrees. With cash advance in hand, the bullfighter meets a friend at a bar. The friend warns him—over and over—that he's too old to get in the ring. “What do you keep on doing it for?” the friend asks.

“I don't know,” the bullfighter says. The next night, he is gored.

About the past, Knoxville is almost mystically serene. He doesn't complain about back pain. He doesn't dwell on mistakes. He's fond of sayings like “The toothpaste is already out of the tube.” Unlike other cast members, he's never once had a nightmare about filming “Jackass.” His wife says that he laughs in his sleep.

When he worries at all, he worries about the future. What will happen now that he can't play the way he used to? Will the appetite fade from want of opportunity or explode from lack of outlet? If Johnny can't run, what's left?

Part of him finds the question ridiculous. These days, Knoxville behaves like a person with plenty to lose. He spends time with his family. He eats protein and steamed vegetables, goes on walks and hikes, drinks water. He takes finasteride to support hair growth. He moisturizes. On a pretty evening in June, with the Cadillac parked near Sunset under a strawberry sky, he talked through the many wonders life has dropped in his lap. “Everything's happened at a fortunate time,” he said, gazing out the window at a man dressed as a pirate. “I'm finally happy. I'm in a really great place. My kids are growing up. They're flourishing. I've met the person I'm supposed to be with. What more can you want?”

He scarcely paused before answering his own question.

“I do miss it sometimes. But I'm trying not to.”

Knoxville doesn't keep track of how many bones he's broken, but he'll tell anyone who listens about his sixteen concussions—not to boast, but from some idea that saying the absurd number out loud will dampen his longing for stunts. “I'm still not there yet, and maybe I never will be,” he said. “I guess it's the price I'll pay for trying to make cartoons come to life.” ❖

item.title: 内塔尼亚胡的高级将军如何成为他最强大的挑战者
item.description:
2026-07-27T10:00:00.000Z

卡法哈纳吉德 (Kfar HaNagid) 是一个温暖、充满马车的夜晚，这个沿海村庄以中世纪安达卢斯地区著名诗人、学者、战士和政治家什穆埃尔·哈纳吉德 (Shmuel HaNagid) 的名字命名。数百名成熟的人群聚集在村庄的绿地上。他们不安地坐在白色塑料椅子上，等待以色列国防军退役参谋长加迪·艾森科特的到来，他目前似乎最有可能取代该国历史上任职时间最长的总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡。选举定于 10 月 27 日举行。艾森科特迟到了。

扩音器里播放着以色列流行歌曲，空气中充满了政治谈话。令人担忧的来源似乎无穷无尽：黎巴嫩北部的战斗；特朗普政府从与德黑兰新政权的疯狂谈判转向长期轰炸行动；内塔尼亚胡与极端正统派进行便利交易，这是他的投票集团的重要组成部分；整个意识形态领域和全世界对以色列的敌意不断加深。在卡法尔哈纳吉德和其他地方，人们很少讨论的是加沙地带巨大的人类苦难和破坏，以及西岸各地村庄的定居者每天对巴勒斯坦人造成的混乱。

艾森科特终于来了。他今年六十六岁，肚子宽阔，表情痛苦。当他微笑时，他会皱起眉头，就像坐骨神经痛一样。他穿着一件深色马球衫，这是他退伍后的制服。艾森科特的父母是收入微薄的摩洛哥移民。他出生在提比里亚，在埃拉特长大，这两个城市被认为位于以色列外围。如果艾森科特获胜，他将成为第一位具有这种背景的总理。

这给内塔尼亚胡带来了一个问题。尽管内塔尼亚胡在耶路撒冷的一个富裕社区长大，而且是西班牙宗教裁判所著名历史学家的德系儿子，但内塔尼亚胡长期以来一直将自己和他的利库德集团定位为工人阶级、虔诚者、无声者和米兹拉希姆人的安全卫士，这些人从穆斯林占主导地位的国家的犹太社区来到以色列。这里的大多数分析人士认为，在势均力敌的选举中，如果艾森科特能够在基里亚特什莫纳、奥法基姆、阿什杜德、纳哈里亚和迪莫纳等省会城市至少吸引一些“软右派”选民，他就能获胜。记者希洛·格雷泽在《国土报》上写道，在利库德集团的许多传统据点中，艾森科特被他的支持者称为“dialina ”，摩洛哥阿拉伯语中“我们中的一个”的意思。

当艾森科特登上一个临时搭建的小舞台时，人群轻轻鼓掌。他解释说，他这一天的大部分时间都在阿什凯隆市度过，在那里他参加了一位名叫大卫·哈祖特的年轻陆军上尉的葬礼，他在黎巴嫩的“黎明前后”的战斗中阵亡。

“我个人并不认识他，但他的家人邀请我参加，”艾森科特说。他的节奏很稳重，语气很严肃。 “他失去了父亲，是母亲唯一的儿子，有一个妹妹。他的母亲同意签署同意书，允许他担任战斗职务，因为他坚持这样做。他自愿加入戈拉尼旅的一支战斗部队。”与会者都知道，这也是艾森科特的服装，也是以色列民粹主义的象征，即“人民旅”。

在接下来的一个小时里，艾森科特发表演讲并回答问题。例行公事。他既没有内塔尼亚胡那样熟练的口才，也没有流利的英语，而且他与梅纳赫姆·贝京等早期时代的煽动者没有什么共同之处。他只是缺乏愚钝，并以此为美德。去年，他成立了一个名为“Yashar”的政党——这个名字的意思是正直、正直、公正。在讲台上，他轻快地阐述了自己的主题和竞选承诺，其中包括承诺让以色列恢复为“犹太、民主、进步和自由的国家”。内塔尼亚胡很少听到这样的说法，更不用说他手下两位最种族主义和反动的部长了：国家安全部长伊塔马尔·本格维尔和财政部长贝扎莱尔·斯莫特里奇。两国都毫无歉意地支持对加沙的种族清洗和吞并西岸。

艾森科特将自己推销为一名卑微的士兵，一个没有腐败或口是心非的政治新手。艾森科特在以色列国防军服役四十一年，包括在内塔尼亚胡手下担任军队最高职位总参谋长，并于 2022 年至 2025 年在以色列议会任职。他说，在这段短暂的任期内，他发现“以色列的民主比我想象的要脆弱得多。”

自一代人前奥斯陆和平进程崩溃和第二次起义爆发以来，民意稳步向右转。按照当代以色列的标准，艾森科特可以被描述为中左翼的小“d”民主党人。在顾问的敦促下，并针对 10 月 7 日之后以色列的政治现实，他正在进一步向中间靠拢。他很少对加沙战争的规模和进行表示保留。他最近称纽约市长佐兰·马姆达尼是反犹太主义者，因为他要求联邦政府根据国际刑事法院的逮捕令逮捕内塔尼亚胡。艾森科特还避免使用两国解决方案的语言，至少作为一种即将到来的可能性。 6月，他对第12频道“会见媒体”节目的采访者说，“我从来没有说过两个国家代表两个民族，因为我了解这种宗教-民族-社会冲突的深度，而任何谈论‘现在和平’和两个国家的人都不理解这种冲突。”

当我关注艾森科特的竞选活动并与他进行详细交谈时，我发现他的吸引力中最具粘性的方面与意识形态或政策几乎没有关系。如果他获胜（考虑到内塔尼亚胡的政治技巧，尽管最近民意调查激增，但这一点还远未确定），那将是因为他在方式和性格上都是反比比的。更重要的是，他向许多以色列人反映了他们自己的一些东西。艾森科特是一个破碎的人。他遭受了巨大的损失。在很大程度上，他是一位政治家，与以色列选民最深厚的联系就是他的悲伤。

2023 年 10 月 7 日早上 6 点 30 分不久，艾森科特正在特拉维夫北部荷兹利亚的家中，此时以色列南部开始传来新闻报道。数千名哈马斯武装分子在努赫巴精英部队的带领下，刚刚突破了加沙围栏的一百多个点。他们乘坐摩托车和皮卡车经陆路、乘坐摩托艇经海上、以及乘坐机动滑翔伞经空中进入以色列。他们以惊人的速度渗透了大约二十个基布兹和斯德洛特小城。一场杀戮开始了。广播和电视很快就有报道称，一些家庭将自己锁在安全的房间里，通过电话寻求帮助。几个小时以来，几乎没有什么进展。

当艾森科特吸收这些第一份报告时，他喊出了他的五个孩子之一，即他 25 岁的儿子盖尔。

“加尔，醒醒，”他说。 “这是战争。”

“你在说什么？”加尔说道。

“这是战争，”艾森科特再次说道。

加尔正在特拉维夫大学学习生物信息学，周末在家。 “他的想法、他的梦想是成为一名医生或科学家，”艾森科特告诉我。

他开车送盖尔到他在特拉维夫的公寓，领取他的制服和装备，然后带他到一个集合点，在那里他与预备役战友会合。加尔接受过战地医疗训练。

四天后，随着对加沙的地面入侵迫在眉睫，并考虑对黎巴嫩真主党发动袭击，内塔尼亚胡要求艾森科特成为一个小型战时内阁的成员。艾森科特曾于2015年2月至2019年1月期间在内塔尼亚胡手下担任总参谋长，但现在是一名政治对手。内塔尼亚胡希望向分裂严重的公众展示统一战线，其中许多人已经开始厌恶和不信任他。经过数月的大规模示威活动反对他削减司法权力的努力后，他迫切需要为即将到来的战争提供支持。在哈马斯袭击之前，包括空军飞行员在内的许多预备役军人曾威胁拒绝服役，以抗议他们认为内塔尼亚胡对以色列民主机构构成的危险。

“我加入了战时内阁，尽管我一生中从未想过自己会与本-格维尔和斯莫特里奇坐在同一张桌子上，”艾森科特告诉我。 “第一次会议”——10 月 11 日——“非常戏剧化。晚上 5 点 Bibi 叫我去参加一个会议。当我走进房间时，我不知道会议会讨论什么。这是 Bibi 第一次意识到失去平衡是什么感觉。这很奇怪。一开始，我不知道我们在做什么。然后我意识到他们叫我去讨论定点清除哈桑·纳斯鲁拉 (Hassan Nasrallah) 的问题，”该组织的领导人真主党。 “我不知道内塔尼亚胡刚刚与拜登通电话，拜登告诉他，‘不要’。”有一个介绍，据说袭击将于晚上7 点进行。总参谋长停止讲话后，内塔尼亚胡转向战时内阁说，“你有什么想法？” ”

以色列情报部门后来获得的文件显示，加沙哈马斯领导人叶海亚·辛瓦尔和其他哈马斯领导人多年来一直与纳斯鲁拉和伊朗政权讨论针对以色列的多线“歼灭计划”。辛瓦尔在没有事先警告盟友的情况下发动了袭击，然后向贝鲁特和德黑兰发出信息，为让他们措手不及而道歉，并恳求他们立即加入战斗。真主党的精锐拉德万部队及其庞大的火箭军火库部署在黎巴嫩南部边境附近，但纳斯鲁拉拒绝仓促介入一场如此严重的战争。他只批准了有限的象征性袭击来支持哈马斯。

在战时内阁中，艾森科特反对开辟第二条战线。 “我说我们必须把重点放在南部，”他回忆道。 “我们需要在那里保持稳定。只有在解决了南部的哈马斯问题后，我们才应该转向北方。”他继续说道，“会议六点结束，我们去了一个地下掩体。当我到达时，有人告诉我，只有一位准将”——军事情报研究部主任阿米特·萨尔——“才真正头脑清醒。其他人都失去了理智。总参谋长说，‘我们必须结束这次谈话，因为在我把飞机送上天之前，我只有二十分钟的时间。’”于是我请这位准将起身到房间里去。萨尔说他认为这将是一个很大的错误。在他的陈述之后，内阁中的其他三人也同意他的观点。”最终，艾森科特的论点获胜了。当飞机在空中飞行时，内塔尼亚胡取消了罢工。

“我们阻止了一个非常错误的决定，因为据《华盛顿邮报》报道，如果我们当时袭击黎巴嫩，我们就会实现辛瓦尔的战略愿景，立即引发地区战争，”艾森科特说。 “哈马斯给我们造成了历史上最大的损失，它本来会成为第二战线。”

会议在午夜时分结束。当艾森科特回家时，他发现手机上有几条来自加尔的消息。

他把儿子叫了回来。 “加尔，这是怎么回事？”他问道。

几年前，当艾森科特对他的家人进行关于从政的民意调查时，加尔告诉他，在军队服役四十年就足够了。他应该享受他的生活。但现在盖尔说：“我明白为什么参与政治对你来说很重要。”

“会议结束后我仍然感到精疲力尽，”艾森科特告诉我。 “我说，‘我想我刚刚做了一些对战争非常重要的事情，稍后我会告诉你。’ ”

在接下来的几周里，艾森科特参与了有关战争行为的激烈辩论。他敦促尽快达成协议，释放尽可能多的人质。人质分散在加沙各地，其中许多人藏在加沙地带地下的隧道网络深处。以色列情报部门认为没有可能大量营救他们。不会出现恩德培式的奇迹。艾森科特认为，让他们回家的唯一方法是将他们的释放作为国家优先事项，并继续与辛瓦尔谈判。斯莫特里奇、本-格维尔和高级军事官员将消灭哈马斯放在首位，不顾平民付出的代价。随着伤亡和破坏的增加，内塔尼亚胡援引了一种开放式的学说，他很快将其称为“全面胜利”。情报报告显示人质遭到虐待，但内塔尼亚胡和他的部长们对他们​​的家人并没有表现出多少同情，他们恳求采取行动释放他们。艾森科特在争论中败诉，最终离开了战时内阁。他说，对于一位主要关心的是维护与本格维尔和斯莫特里奇的联盟以及他自己的政治权力的总理来说，他不能再充当“遮羞布”。

十一月下旬的一个星期四，盖尔休完预备役回家休息。近一周以来，人质协议使战斗暂停，并释放了数十名俘虏。第二天早上暂停结束。那天晚上，加尔和父母一起吃了安息日晚餐。周六早些时候，艾森科特开车送他去了特拉维夫，在那里他可以乘公共汽车前往集合点。他们大部分时间都是默默地骑行。盖尔和他的朋友们一直熬夜到凌晨4:30。当他和父亲最终到达特拉维夫时，他们拥抱并说再见。

12月第一周的一天早上，艾森科特参观了加沙边境的一个基地，听取了有关在加沙地带没收的爆炸物的情况介绍。在师部，一名将军突然把他从房间里拉出来，并说加尔“受了重伤”。艾森科特应该立即回家。艾森科特此前曾多次传递过这样的信息。 “请相信我，”他告诉将军。他明白，他的儿子已经死了。

“那一刻，”他回忆道，“我切换到了自动驾驶模式。”在一种恍惚的状态下，他上了车，向北前往荷兹利亚。他一边开车，一边打电话给他的大儿子盖伊，说道：“盖尔被杀了。回家吧，确保在我到达之前没有人进入房子。”

三点过后，艾森科特回到家。他的妻子汉娜正在让孙女睡觉。他的三个女儿也在那里。他告诉他们他所了解到的发生的事情。情报官员发现，哈马斯在加沙地带北部贾巴利亚郊区扣押了两名阵亡以色列人的遗体——一名名叫齐夫·达多(Ziv Dado)的士兵和一名名叫伊登·扎卡里亚(Eden Zakaria)的年轻女子，她们曾参加过诺瓦音乐节。加尔和另一名士兵埃亚尔·伯科维茨 (Eyal Berkowitz) 共同努力寻找并救出这两具尸体。行动中，加尔和“贝尔科”被简易爆炸装置炸死。救援成功，但值得吗？ “我的妻子问了我很多关于这次任务的棘手问题，”艾森科特告诉我。 “冒着士兵的危险去营救死去的人质是正确的吗？她已经问过我很多次了。”

数千人涌入荷兹利亚的军人公墓参加加尔的葬礼。内塔尼亚胡和以色列的大部分政治和安全机构都在那里。艾森科特告诉我，他已经五十年没有哭过，但是，当他站在儿子铺着旗帜的棺材前向聚集的人讲话时，他有时无法继续下去。

“加卢什，我们亲爱的，”他说，“我向你保证，我们将继续成为一个团结而幸福的家庭，这样你和其他阵亡者的牺牲就不会白费，我们也配得上这些牺牲。我向你致敬，心爱的儿子。”然后，艾森科特戴着墨镜，声音沙哑，对哀悼者们说道：“痛苦是巨大的。巨大的。但我们是一个幸福、坚强的家庭，如果盖尔能再告诉我一件事，他会说，‘选择生活——保持快乐。’”他和我们一起住在我们心里。生活中的他就是这样的。他对我们来说将永远如此。”

不久之后，电视记者伊拉娜·达扬 (Ilana Dayan) 在第 12 频道采访了艾森科特，询问他和家人如何承受失去亲人的痛苦。

“早晨和夜晚变得更加艰难，”他说，“但至少就我而言，没有其他选择，因为我知道其他选择对我个人和家庭都不利。睡觉前和起床时，它都伴随着我。但我真的希望我能学会忍受它。我必须这样做。选择就是一个深渊。”

损失接连不断：艾森科特的两个侄子也在战斗中阵亡，一个在汗尤尼斯，另一个在拜特拉希亚。很长一段时间，艾森科特都处于哀悼之中，精疲力尽，推迟了所有的政治决定。随后他于2025年7月离开民族团结党，两个月后成立亚沙尔党，并于2026年6月30日正式宣布打算接替内塔尼亚胡担任总理。

10 月 7 日哈马斯袭击事件发生后，两个提议在以色列公共话语中被视为近乎公理。

首先是内塔尼亚胡不可能继续担任总理。毕竟，他主持了该国历史上最严重的国家安全崩溃。内塔尼亚胡把自己塑造成以色列的丘吉尔，他专注于伊朗，同时对真实和想象的敌人发动一场明显的特朗普式文化战争：媒体、文化精英以及法院和军队中所谓的深层国家对手。他认为哈马斯——尤其是与黎巴嫩真主党或德黑兰政权相比——是一支乌合之众、歹徒和持有 AK-47 步枪的狂热分子，可以通过卡塔尔的现金注入、先进的电子监控和定期的有限战争（一种被称为“除草”的策略）来遏制他们。大屠杀发生一周内，民意调查显示，没有做出任何悔罪姿态的内塔尼亚胡几乎肯定会失去权力。他可能的继任者是前将军、以色列国防军领导人本尼·甘茨，他身材高大、满头银发、沉默寡言，以至于唐纳德·特朗普肯定会认为他是“直接从中央选角中脱颖而出”。

内塔尼亚胡面临着街头和政府内部的愤怒。中左翼反对党 Yesh Atid 党魁、2022 年担任总理六个月的亚伊尔·拉皮德 (Yair Lapid) 为我回忆起袭击发生后他在内塔尼亚胡在议会时发表的一次讲话。 “首相先生，令人惊奇的是你还是不明白。”拉皮德说道，声音里充满了轻蔑。 “你将一无所有。不会有以你名字命名的博物馆，没有广场。甚至不会有本杰明·内塔尼亚胡喷泉。只会发生一件事：10月7日……你的时间到了。你的极端主义和鲁莽的政府正在崩溃。在你脚下，大地正在燃烧。”

然而内塔尼亚胡继续发动战争，同时拒绝承认他在战争起源中所扮演的角色。由于缺乏信息和生动的公众形象，对甘茨的支持逐渐减少。因此，尽管首相的地位有所下降，而且艾森科特最近也取得了上升，但他很有可能在今年秋天连任。他的方法将为美国人所熟悉。他靠纯粹的煽动和迎合顽固的“让美国再次伟大”的基础，纵容极端主义部长追求吞并和种族清洗，并接受极端正统派的要求，免除兵役和持续获得巨额国家补贴而生存。

内塔尼亚胡的反对者认为，这种生存策略终于站不住脚了。 “比比认为他可以继续骑虎难下，”拉皮德告诉我。 “他认为他可以骑乘犹太极端主义的老虎——但犹太极端主义骑乘了他。他认为他可以骑乘宗教权力的老虎——但宗教权力骑乘了他。”

即便如此，反对派仍然感到焦虑。 2006年至2009年担任总理的埃胡德·奥尔默特告诉我，内塔尼亚胡的许多反对者担心他可能会效仿特朗普的做法，试图抹黑选举结果。 “这里的警察管理不正常，”奥尔默特说。本-格维尔担任国家安全部长，负责监督警察。 “如果比比失败，他们将如何执行选举？”奥尔默特继续说道。 “他可能会尝试不承认选票，就像他的朋友特朗普在一月六日所做的那样。”

如果内塔尼亚胡获胜，艾森科特、奥尔默特、拉皮德和我采访过的许多其他人预计以色列的孤立将会加深，许多最有才华和生产力的公民，特别是那些拥有第二本护照的公民，将考虑他们的选择。奥尔默特说：“如果比比赢得选举，我认为十万人，从二十五岁到四十岁不等，包括高科技人员、带孩子的学者，将迅速离开这个国家。”

“我认为以色列已经失去了理智，就像9/11之后的美国一样，”特拉维夫大学哲学教授、民主活动家阿萨夫·沙龙告诉我。 “我有生以来第一次不再相信这个国家能够生存。我一直讨厌这种危言耸听。但以色列已经把自己逼到了一个国家生存受到切实威胁的境地。”

美国民主党建制派的一位资深人士最近表达了这种担忧。 7月初，比尔·克林顿和巴拉克·奥巴马的前高级顾问拉姆·伊曼纽尔来到特拉维夫大学，谴责内塔尼亚胡领导他的国家陷入“占领与孤立”的灾难性死胡同。他警告说，以色列不仅失去了民主党，而且失去了民主党。它有失去美国的危险。 “追求所谓的大以色列就像‘从河流到海洋’的口号一样自我毁灭和狂热，”伊曼纽尔说。 “你们的政府是目前约旦河西岸无辜家庭所遭受的恐怖的同谋。这损害了你们作为一个小国的国际合法性，而在你们最无力承担的时候。”这种药特别严厉，因为它来自一个很难被视为激进分子或反犹太分子的人。伊曼纽尔的父亲参加了 1948 年的独立战争。他的中间名是以色列。

10 月 7 日之后的第二个前提是，出于良心和传统，内塔尼亚胡将被迫成立一个正式调查委员会，调查灾难性安全失败的根源。该委员会以 1973 年 10 月埃及和叙利亚在赎罪日突然入侵后，由以色列最高法院首席法官西蒙·阿格拉纳特 (Shimon Agranat) 主持的委员会为蓝本。阿格拉纳特委员会发现了遗漏的线索和被忽视的警告，从而暴露了安全机构的粗心大意。这个国家已经开始研究这个空白。如果以色列坦克部队在西奈半岛和戈兰高地遭受数天的惨重损失后没有重新集结，埃及和叙利亚军队很可能会占领以色列中部。该报告促使许多高级安全和情报官员辞职，并帮助结束了果尔达·梅厄的政治生涯。

然而，内塔尼亚胡永远不会以这种方式承担责任。多位高级军事和情报官员相继辞职，并发表声明对自己 10 月 7 日之前和 10 月 7 日的失败深表遗憾。他们所服务的政府首脑内塔尼亚胡拒绝这样做。他轻描淡写地指出，富兰克林·罗斯福在珍珠港事件后没有辞职，乔治·W·布什在 9/11 事件后也没有下台。他们专注于眼前的战争。内塔尼亚胡的不道歉是一种转移注意力的做法。

内塔尼亚胡公开与有关“内部叛徒”的猖獗言论保持距离，但他几乎没有采取任何措施来遏制这种言论在他的政治阵营内外的蔓延。这一系列阴谋论认为，高级军事和情报官员故意未能及时叫醒他，以阻止哈马斯入侵。根据赖克曼大学进行的一项调查，在 2022 年投票支持内塔尼亚胡联盟的人中，多达一半的人开始相信这种深层国家理论。这些理论的传播者包括对内塔尼亚胡友好的第 14 频道的评论员，以及内塔尼亚胡的儿子亚伊尔 (Yair)。亚伊尔是一名播客兼社交媒体炸弹投掷者，他将小唐纳德·特朗普的血腥忠诚与劳拉·卢默的垃圾贴能量融为一体。以色列议会利库德集团成员塔利·戈特利夫错误地声称，美国情报部门截获了左翼抗议领袖希克马·布雷斯勒的搭档与策划这次袭击的哈马斯领导人辛瓦尔之间的电话。

“在美国，这比 9/11 阴谋论更为普遍，而且不难找出原因，”记者阿莫斯·哈雷尔 (Amos Harel) 告诉我。 “如果你相信比比是上帝，就很难向自己解释发生了什么。这一切怎么会如此彻底地崩溃？需要有人受到责备。”

尽管内塔尼亚胡口头上表示应该对安全失误进行调查，但很少有以色列人期望他建立一个独立的国家调查委员会。在无人参与的情况下， 《国土报》的长期国防分析师哈雷尔亲自完成了大部分前期工作。他最近的畅销书《06:29：剖析失败》是对傲慢、忽视和制度自满的四百页控诉书。他缺乏官方委员会的传票权，但他在国家安全机构中的广泛消息来源使他能够重建警告如何一再被忽视，以及一种完全误读加沙局势的主导假设（概念）如何占据主导地位。

哈雷尔描述了包括驻扎在加沙附近的女性地面观察员在内的初级军官如何在围栏被冲破之前就发现了重大袭击的迹象，但他们的报告却被上级忽视了。情报官员还注意到，哈马斯在入侵前几个小时就激活了以色列的SIM卡。但高级官员得出的结论是，哈马斯正在进行演习，或者最多准备发动有限的袭击。

加沙境内出现异常活动迹象后，哈雷尔还重建了高级军事和情报官员在六日和七日晚上的磋商情况。该国内部安全部门辛贝特 (Shin Bet) 负责人罗南·巴尔 (Ronen Bar) 和总参谋长赫兹·哈勒维 (Herzi Halevi) 都在深夜接到电话。这些报道足以令人震惊，哈勒维给自己写了一张便条：“我们不要让自己相信这没什么。”凌晨5 点 49 分左右，以色列监控系统在安全屏障附近发现骑摩托车和吉普车的男子。但仍没有采取有效措施。

“当我读到袭击前发生的事情的笔录时，我真想把头撞到墙上，”哈雷尔告诉我。

艾森科特和其他反对派领导人——包括拉皮德、中右翼前总理纳夫塔利·贝内特和左倾民主党的亚尔·戈兰——一致认为，新联合政府的首要行动之一应该是成立一个持续到 10 月 7 日的国家调查委员会。内塔尼亚胡声称他的情报负责人只是没有叫醒他，这一说法不太可能对调查人员产生多大影响。

“在指挥系统中，不知道并不能免除责任。恰恰相反，它会增加责任，”艾森科特说。 “总理排在第一位，他从军事情报部门和以色列国防军那里获得最新消息，他也参与其中……因此，当他根据圣经宣誓就职时，责任就交给了他。他承担着尖锐而明确的责任。你不必承担责任。责任就在那里。”

艾森科特对指挥责任的坚持有一个明显的局限性。他仍然不愿就加沙战争的异常严重性和持续时间对内塔尼亚胡进行任何细节谴责。 “战争开始后，以色列人第一次开始谈论大屠杀，”他说。 “人们开始说，‘哈马斯是纳粹。’人们确信发生了屠杀、强奸和可怕的事情，每个人都知道这一点而卷入了战争。因此，像加尔这样的人愿意付出一切，包括生命，以便国家能够继续存在。 。 。 。但不可否认的是，10 月 7 日战争开始后，以色列的心态开始向右转。我留在同一个地方。但我明白，如果以色列一开始不采取重拳打击并展示实力，那么我们在这里就没有未来。”

这是我自 2023 年 10 月以来第五次访问以色列。当我上次访问时，即去年 6 月，内塔尼亚胡和他的支持者辩称，哈马斯已被彻底击败，以色列已利用其军事力量重塑该地区。他们毫不讽刺地谈到了“新中东”，前总理西蒙·佩雷斯曾用这个词来描述一个和平的未来，在这个未来中，以色列最终将与邻国（包括新生的巴勒斯坦国）在政治和经济上和谐相处。

当两人成为政治对手时，内塔尼亚胡嘲笑佩雷斯与该地区的残酷现实完全脱节。现在，在 2025 年夏天，内塔尼亚胡和他的阵营设想了一种不同的“新中东”，在这个中东，以色列从灾难中恢复过来，粉碎了真主党，并利用特朗普派遣的美国 B-2 轰炸机摧毁了伊朗核项目，总统宣布该项目“被消灭”。他们预测伊朗将爆发民众起义，伊斯兰神权政治即将崩溃。黎巴嫩和叙利亚肯定会实现稳定，《亚伯拉罕协议》将扩大到包括更多逊尼派国家，其中包括沙特阿拉伯。曾担任内塔尼亚胡驻华盛顿大使的迈克尔·奥伦当时告诉我，“如果不了解十二天战争，你很可能无法了解二十一世纪。”

Entirely absent from this euphoric, triumphalist, end-of-history vision was any acknowledgment of the deaths of at least seventy thousand Palestinians, including more than twenty thousand children; the complete destruction of the vast majority of housing, schools, and hospitals throughout the Gaza Strip; and the many other acts committed there that constitute war crimes. Nor did it anticipate that Netanyahu and Trump would embark on a reckless new war. By the time I returned, months of Israeli bombardment had killed thousands of people in Lebanon and driven some 1.2 million people from their homes. A year after the Twelve-Day War, Oren allowed, “That was the glass-half-full version of things.”

Eisenkot, for his part, regards Netanyahu's declaration of victory in Iran as ludicrous. After watching Netanyahu make the claim one night on Channel 14, he called one of his advisers and said, “Does Bibi really think everyone here is stupid?”

Danny Citrinowicz, who spent twenty-five years in military command positions, including as head of the Iran branch of military intelligence, was sharper still. “Israel, in its wounded rage after October 7th, lost its strategic mind,” he told me. The joint Trump-Netanyahu military campaign ended in “an absolute disaster,” he said. The bombing on the first day killed the aging Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was succeeded by his even more hard-line son, Mojtaba, and left the leadership of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps more radicalized and empowered than ever. The hope that bombing might inspire a rapid popular uprising was “preposterous from the start.”

In the end, Citrinowicz told me, “we ended up giving even greater legitimacy to the Iranian regime and strengthening them.” The Gulf states, which had been drawing closer to Israel and the United States, would now seek an accommodation with Iran. Trump had imagined that he could replicate the ease of the American operation in Venezuela. Instead, he launched an air campaign against a country of more than ninety million people and found himself in a quagmire that was fracturing the MAGA coalition and threatening the global economy. Netanyahu, who had sold the plan to Trump after failing to do so with American Presidents going back to George W. Bush, now faced an Iranian leadership with a stronger motive to acquire a nuclear weapon. And US support for Israel had cratered across the political spectrum, a development that most Israelis had yet to grasp fully.

“Most Israelis cannot bear to hear Israeli policy criticized abroad, and so many of them turn around and assume it is antisemitism,” Citrinowicz told me. “Antisemitism exists, but you can't be so defensive to think that any and all criticism comes from that place.”

Yet most Israelis, despite their generally favorable view of Trump, believe that the American President ended the campaign too soon and failed them. “The bottom line was a lack of American will,” Oren insisted.

Amit Segal, a conservative commentator for Channel 12 and Israel Hayom , told me that Netanyahu regards renewed conflict with Iran as politically advantageous. “For Trump, ending the war with Iran is a crucial condition for the midterms,” Segal told me. “For Netanyahu, ending the war is the obstacle to winning the 2026 election. From a political perspective, this is why there is a divide between them.”

When it became clear that Eisenkot would be a leading candidate for Prime Minister, the producers of “Uvda,” Channel 12's investigative-news program, made an hour-long documentary about the early stages of his campaign. It was a traditional fly-on-the-wall piece, though, in this case, the fly generally buzzed around Eisenkot's car as he was ferried from one campaign stop to another. He sat in the front passenger seat, displaying a kind of wry detachment from the patter and questions directed at him. Eisenkot does not hesitate to describe himself as fat, and he cheerfully admitted to his fellow-passengers that he had recently lost a few kilos through a combination of diet, exercise, and “the shot.”

“All of his rivals may be slicker than him,” the narrator intoned early on, but Eisenkot “has a stronger story.” The story, of course, was that of the honest military man and the grieving father.

The question posed by the documentary, and daily in the Israeli press, is whether Eisenkot has what it takes to defeat Netanyahu. In a typical scene, Eisenkot visited the Tel Aviv apartment of Ronni and Shelly Zehavi, a prosperous couple who made their money in tech, and met with their equally prosperous friends. As he girded himself for a polite assault from these potential donors, the narrator said that the “elephant in the room” needed to be addressed. The country, Eisenkot allowed, had grown accustomed to a cunning politician “who knows how to deliver a message, talk, and connect.” If Netanyahu were to win, one guest warned, “half the kids of the people in this room won't be here in twenty years.” They worried that Eisenkot, for all his years in the military, was “too polite.” (Israelis do not, in the main, value politesse.) One potential donor told him to “wake up” and “stop fumbling.”

At a humbler gathering of predominantly Moroccan Jews, the message was much the same. “The gloves have to come off,” one woman told him. “This is the moment.”

In another scene, filmed at campaign headquarters, Eisenkot and his advisers were being tutored by Steve Miller, a protégé of the late Arthur Finkelstein, an American political consultant who worked closely with Netanyahu. In the 1996 campaign, Finkelstein supplied Netanyahu with the hot-button slogans “Peres will divide Jerusalem” and “Bibi is good for the Jews.” They exemplified his method of turning political disagreement into a stark choice between security and betrayal. Miller lectured Eisenkot and his advisers on the art of political positioning. Using a left-to-right axis, he made clear that Eisenkot would be wise to edge rightward to win voters on the center-right.

“What defines right and left—the Palestinians?” Eisenkot asked. Such questions, though, were anathema in mainstream political conversations after October 7th. Even Yair Golan, who would occupy the left flank of any opposition coalition led by Eisenkot, told me that although he was prepared to speak of two states as an eventual goal, the other opposition leaders were far more circumspect. Ultimately, Golan said, the choice facing Israelis is “annexation or separation.” That is no secret to anyone.

Recent months had brought intense jockeying within the opposition. The former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, seeking to return to the office, had hoped to lead a broad alliance that included Golan, Lapid, Eisenkot, and Avigdor Lieberman, a hawk with strong support among immigrants from the former Soviet Union. Bennett had once led the Yesha Council, the settlers' umbrella organization, and later served as Netanyahu's minister of the economy. His party rose for a time in the polls, but Eisenkot was cool to the idea of accepting a subordinate role, and when Bennett and Lapid formed an alliance in April, under the name Beyachad, or Together, they gave him a last chance to join.他拒绝了。 His calculation was easy to discern: Why Bennett and not him?

The polls soon exposed Bennett's vulnerability. His alliance with Lapid cost him support on the right, while his hold on centrist voters had never been secure. (It was through the vagaries of coalition politics that Bennett had managed to become Prime Minister, in 2021, despite the fact that his party commanded just seven of the Knesset's hundred and twenty seats.)

People in Bennett's campaign were eager to warn me that, with Eisenkot as the opposition's leading figure, the election could become a “rerun” of previous challenges to Netanyahu led by center-left politicians: Gantz, Lapid, Tzipi Livni, and Isaac Herzog. “Gadi has a high sympathy rate, he lost his son, he's a likable guy,” a campaign source said. “They think that will do the job.” Bennett himself emphasized his own right-wing credentials on security. “If we want to win, we have to unite,” he told me. “We have to learn from the mistakes of previous elections and get into a room and decide things until the smoke comes out. It's still early.”

Eisenkot agreed about the need for unity, but he smiled and made clear that, in his mind, the leadership question had already been settled. He was even predicting what Netanyahu would do after losing. “I believe he'll take his package, like Viktor Orbán did,” he told me. “I don't think he will stay in the opposition. I think he will retire.”

Others were less certain. A source close to the Prime Minister described Israeli coalition politics to me as a “circus.” Eisenkot could emerge from the election as the opposition's dominant figure and still fail to assemble a government. “And then, who knows?”

If Netanyahu did leave the scene, Eisenkot said, Israel would at least have a chance to ease its polarization and repair its standing abroad. This was the core of his immediate ambition. “We have an opportunity now to build a real Jewish state,” he said. “We'll have the ability to correct the terrible division created during Netanyahu's reign and bring Israel back to the values of David Ben-Gurion,” a founder of the nation and its first Prime Minister.

Eisenkot's campaign headquarters occupies the second floor of a high-rise in Ramat HaSharon, north of Tel Aviv. His campaign manager, Ronen Manelis, is an astute former military-intelligence officer of Russian descent who first served under him during the second intifada near Nablus and later at the Kirya, the military complex in Tel Aviv. A brigadier general, Manelis was also the spokesman for the IDF from 2017 to 2019. He is unabashed about selling a visitor on his candidate.

“Gadi has the gravitas to do this step-by-step work,” Manelis told me on my first visit to Ramat HaSharon. “He is one of the cleverest people in Israel. He is shrewd, more of a politician than people think. He is lovable. People come up and kiss him. A cabdriver tells me he is kadosh , holy, like a god. He is what the country needs. This is Biden against Trump in 2020, a fight for the soul of the nation. The only one who can do it is Gadi. If we lose it, I am not sure we will have another chance.”

He barely paused for breath. “For a generation, we've really known only one Prime Minister. So people believe you need the fluent English. The makeup. The teleprompter. The standing ovations in Congress. But we need something else. We need the antithesis.”

等等。 Eventually, Manelis exhausted his urge to propagandize and began to show off his other role: the hard man prepared to fight Netanyahu with his own weapons. When I asked him about employing one of Arthur Finkelstein's epigones, he smiled and noted that several members of the staff had worked in Netanyahu's circle. He expressed admiration for Jonatan Urich, a Netanyahu media adviser who has been the subject of three criminal investigations.

“Look, you can't beat them if you don't play their game,” Manelis said. “Unfortunately, Bibi succeeded with all this shit. If I want to win, I need people who know how to succeed.” He did not care if the left-leaning Haaretz criticized the campaign for adopting Finkelstein's methods: “We're not going to beat Netanyahu appealing only to Haaretz readers. We need to bring voters from between the blocs.”

By now, anyone in Israeli public life can anticipate Netanyahu's ugliest lines of attack. Chief among them will be an attempt to brand Eisenkot as pro-Arab. In an earlier election, Netanyahu warned that Arab voters were “coming in droves” to vote for the opposition. The tactic combines racism with hypocrisy. Although Palestinian Arabs make up roughly a fifth of Israel's population, forming a government dependent on Arab parties remains widely regarded as politically illegitimate. Still, Netanyahu himself explored the possibility of bringing into his coalition Mansour Abbas, the head of Ra'am, an Islamist Arab party in the Knesset, before Abbas instead joined the short-lived government led by Bennett and Lapid.

None of this will prevent Netanyahu from using the same weapon again. The most effective instrument of his so-called “poison machine” is Channel 14, an outlet that makes Fox News look like “Democracy Now!” For a time, the channel seemed reluctant to attack the father of a fallen soldier.不再。 Recently, it assailed Eisenkot's campaign for the sin of courting Arab voters.

Eisenkot's military record offers no certain protection from right-wing condemnation. In addition to having been Netanyahu's highest-ranking military commander, he served in Lebanon and the West Bank. He is closely associated with the Dahiya doctrine, which calls for the use of overwhelming and disproportionate force against areas from which hostile organizations operate, including extensive destruction of civilian infrastructure. (Dahiya refers to the predominantly Shiite southern suburbs of Beirut, where Hezbollah established one of its main strongholds.) But, in contemporary Israel, long service in the military or intelligence establishment can indicate a suspicious degree of moderation. Many former commanders, shaped by decades of fighting terrorism and watching negotiations fail, have concluded that two sovereign states or some form of separation from the Palestinians is essential, both as a moral principle and as a practical means of Israeli survival. Netanyahu will portray Eisenkot as belonging to that tribe. “In the past, a general always got his falafel for free,” Nadav Eyal, a columnist for Yedioth Ahronoth , a major Israeli daily, told me. “Not today. Today, he is considered a lefty.”

The campaign expects Netanyahu to use Eisenkot's long military career against him. One example is the so-called Azaria affair. In 2016, an Israeli soldier named Elor Azaria shot and killed a wounded Palestinian assailant who lay incapacitated on the ground. Eisenkot said that Azaria had violated the ethics of the Army, and backed his prosecution. Netanyahu, after seeing support for the soldier swell on social media, spoke with Azaria's father and urged “balance” in the proceedings.

Manelis does not hesitate to turn his candidate's bereavement into a political credential. “The fact that his son died is insurance that he won't do things that are dangerous for the nation,” he told me. Manelis regards it as his job to prevent Netanyahu from defining Eisenkot first. With an air of mischief and pride, he took out his phone and showed me a video on Instagram featuring a Likud jingle sung in Arabic and a reminder of Netanyahu's courtship of Mansour Abbas. “I don't think it's racist,” Manelis said. “We are using his terms—and we need to win.”

He then showed me another campaign video. It reprises a Netanyahu ad from the 2015 campaign—“You will decide who will defend your children!”—while, thanks to AI, Netanyahu wanders through the charred remains of kibbutzim torched by Hamas three years ago. “If you want to lose,” Manelis told me, “don't use someone close to Arthur Finkelstein, don't do a negative campaign, speak only about the Palestinian issue, and say you love Mansour Abbas. Then see what happens in the fall.”

As if to prove Manelis's point about the inevitability of a brutal confrontation, the Netanyahu campaign put out an AI-generated video in mid-July that seemed to transgress every boundary of taste and decency. The clip, which Netanyahu himself posted, showed Eisenkot running through a meadow toward a young man wearing a T-shirt with the motto “Israeli Unity” emblazoned on it. But Eisenkot ignores the young man and instead runs past him to embrace Mansour Abbas. News accounts throughout Israel noted that the young man resembled Eisenkot's late son, Gal. Einav Zangauker, the mother of a son who had been held hostage in Gaza and a former supporter of the Prime Minister, was among the many in Israel who considered the video both despicable and typical of Netanyahu's campaign tactics. “When the video started playing and I saw Gadi running with open arms, the thought crossed my mind that, from the other side, we'd see his late son Gal running into his father's arms,” she wrote on X. “A hug like that would have warmed the heart. But what was I thinking? This is Netanyahu.”

One uncertainty haunting the Eisenkot campaign is Donald Trump. Will the American President intervene at the last moment to help Netanyahu? Manelis wondered whether Trump might do for Netanyahu what J. D. Vance had tried to do for Viktor Orbán by campaigning for him in Budapest. Yet it was unclear how much warmth, if any, remained in the relationship. Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan's recent book, “Regime Change,” recounts a chilling telephone call in which Trump turned against Netanyahu: “Everybody's sick of you, Bibi. All the Jews are sick of you. Even the two Jews on this call are sick of you.” Manelis remains mindful of the President's unpredictability; Trump may still prefer the devil he knows. “The game changer could be the Trump Administration,” he told me.

Campaigns live from moment to moment, poll to poll. Eisenkot and the opposition as a whole were on the rise. One evening, Eisenkot's chief of staff, Noam Bar-Lev, handed Manelis her phone. He glanced at the screen and smiled broadly.

“Amazing,” he said. “We had a good day on Polymarket!”

It was a hot summer morning on the road to Hebron, the second-largest city in the West Bank, after East Jerusalem. I was riding along with Yehuda Shaul, who served in Hebron in the IDF during the second intifada. Later, in his disillusionment, he helped organize Breaking the Silence, an activist organization of Army veterans who document instances of settler violence and evidence of Israel's increasingly blatant attempt to absorb Palestinian land in the occupied territories without formally annexing it. The Tarqumiya checkpoint, which used to be crowded with Palestinians entering and leaving the West Bank in the south, was quiet. Since October 7th, Israeli security forces have cracked down on the movement of Palestinians throughout the West Bank. At the same time, there has been an alarming spike in settler violence across the region, from the villages near Jenin in the north to the Hebron Hills in the south. Young, armed settlers, many of them from small encampments and bent on intimidating Palestinian villagers, stage raids, slaughter farm animals, commit arson, and, all too often, inflict physical mayhem. Palestinians know that they can expect little help from Israeli forces, and still less from the police, which fall under Itamar Ben-Gvir's ministry.

I've visited Hebron many times over the years, and it seems only more menacing now. Large sections of town are ghostly quiet. Army troops enforce strict, perversely precise rules about where Palestinians may, or may not, walk and drive. There is a bewildering maze of “sterile” streets. And the Arabs in town rarely test the litany of restrictions. “For now, they look at Gaza and they know that Israelis behaved this way—there was no check on Israeli cruelty,” Shaul said. “But there will come a moment when the young Palestinians say, 'Why are we accepting this?' This is a disaster waiting to happen, and I fear it will be like Rafah.”

There are two hundred and thirty thousand Palestinians in Hebron; roughly eight hundred Jewish settlers are protected by an entire Army battalion. In Kiryat Arba, the major Jewish settlement in greater Hebron, there are around eight thousand souls, including Ben-Gvir himself. Shaul and I briefly stopped outside Ben-Gvir's house, which is heavily guarded by armed security. He lives there with his wife, Ayala, and their children. It is said that on their first date they visited the nearby grave of Baruch Goldstein, an American-born physician and settler. On February 25, 1994, Goldstein opened fire with an assault rifle on a crowd of Palestinians at prayer, killing twenty-nine and wounding a hundred and twenty-five.

Hebron is the Belfast of the West Bank—a place with far too much history, bloodshed, and religious fervor and not enough geography. For Jews, the massacre of 1929 was yesterday. For Palestinians, Goldstein lives. The Greater Israel movement gained one of its most consequential early footholds in Hebron, in April, 1968, when Moshe Levinger, an Orthodox rabbi, and a small group of followers posing as Swiss tourists arrived at the Arab-owned Park Hotel for a Passover Seder. This was less than a year after Israel's victory in the Six-Day War, and its seizure of Gaza from the Egyptians and the West Bank and East Jerusalem from Jordan. After the holiday, Levinger and his followers refused to leave—and, in effect, they never did, eventually establishing Kiryat Arba. This was an act that they regarded as similar to Abraham's acquisition of the Cave of the Patriarchs during the Bronze Age.

“The uniqueness of Hebron is in its spiritual essence, rooted in the dawn of our national history,” Moshe Mayefsky, the official historian of Kiryat Arba, wrote. “The acquisition of the Land of Israel in its practical sense first took place here.” This manner of settlement—seizure followed by the eventual acquiescence of the government—is part of a pattern that has characterized the occupation of the West Bank ever since.

In the late seventies, the Israeli journalist and historian Amos Elon interviewed Levinger in Hebron. He asked the rabbi if he favored giving the vote to the Arabs in Greater Israel. Levinger replied, “I agree the Arabs were also made in God's image. The trouble is, they're opposed to this being a Jewish state. Therefore, the Jewishness of this state must take precedence in value over their being created in the divine image. . . . Democracy must be subordinated to Israel's national and religious purposes. Do they grant civil rights to thieves and robbers in the United States?”

Levinger's legal adviser, Elyakim Haetzni, told Elon that he had left his law practice and leased his house in Tel Aviv to move to Hebron. “I am a deliriously happy man,” he told Elon. “The Land is here , in Kiryat Arba, not in Tel Aviv. . . . Kiryat Arba does not exist to defend Tel Aviv from Arab attack, but the other way round. Tel Aviv exists to protect Kiryat Arba.”

As Shaul and I walked through Hebron and discussed the recent surge in settler violence, he recalled his own service there as a young soldier. The Israelis conducted nighttime raids meant to intimidate the population, a practice they called “making our presence known.” Now, with Ben-Gvir and Smotrich exercising broad power over the West Bank, the atmosphere was immeasurably more ominous.

“Have you ever seen an anti-colonial struggle where the native population is the majority and gives up?” Shaul said. “This is not the American Indians. The quiet in Hebron is camouflage. Look at the numbers. This is not China and Tibet. Israel doesn't have tens of millions of Jews to overwhelm the Palestinians. The ruthless geographical policies are a sign of weakness in the face of demography. That's how a minority rules.”

His foreboding echoed what I had heard in Jaffa, from Rula Daood, one of the leaders of A Place for Us All, a small Arab-Jewish party. “Something will explode,” she said. “You can't take the rights of people and think they will sit quietly.” Daood recalled seeing a settler strip naked on the street in Hebron, deliberately affronting the religious Muslims around him. “It is another way of conquering the land,” she told me.

Shaul and I drove out of Hebron and into the parched hills toward the village of Susya. Shepherds tended small flocks beside a road leading to a cluster of ramshackle dwellings. There we met Nasser Nawaja, an impassive man in his early forties who works as a field researcher for the human-rights group B'Tselem. He spends his days recording acts of settler violence in the hills and estimates that an incident occurs somewhere in the area every few hours.

Nawaja was born in 1982 in a cave in Old Susya. Four years later, after the Israeli authorities declared the village an archeological site, his family was among the residents expelled from their homes. Nawaja said that the most formative experience of his life came years later, when, at the age of seventeen, he was arrested with several other villagers. They were accused of a killing about which they knew nothing, and were interrogated through the night, bent over, “our noses and mouths in the dirt.”

“In the morning, they realized that we had nothing to do with it and they released us,” Nawaja said. “We approached the ridge near our house—and I didn't see our village! Where were our tents and our homes? When I got here, I saw people crying and faces black with dirt. The IDF came and demolished the whole village. More than thirty families. Right where we are sitting now.”

He recalled, “I was full of hatred. If you had given me a suicide belt, I hated Jews, I would go do it at that moment. I slept one night here, and I thought about what I went through and about revenge. The next morning, a bunch of Jews came here, buses of Jewish activists who came to rebuild our homes. It shakes your brain! Who are they? Collaborators? Just yesterday, Jews had destroyed our homes. That made me think. That's when I understood ultimately that I was at a junction between becoming violent or taking a different path toward nonviolence. I chose that path.”

The path has been difficult. Nawaja cares for an ailing, elderly father and a five-year-old daughter with profound physical and cognitive disabilities. He said that he has repeatedly been arrested and detained, and is barred from visiting the Al-Aqsa Mosque, in Jerusalem. “I am an enemy of the occupying regime,” he said. “And, on the Palestinian side, you always feel you need to explain your position to those who don't understand Jewish and Palestinian activists.”

When Nawaja and other activists call the police to report settler vandalism or violence, the officers sometimes take the activists themselves to a nearby base and interrogate them for hours. Police officers and settlers are often connected by friendship or family ties. “They treat animals better than they treat us,” Nawaja said.

The plan, Nawaja believed, was clear: to “embitter” the lives of the more than three million Palestinians in the West Bank and, when the political circumstances permitted, annex the territory to a Greater Israel. It was the future that Moshe Levinger had imagined decades earlier.

Nawaja regards October 7th as having provided a “golden opportunity” for the radical right to advance its agenda. He is gravely concerned that, even if the October election ends the government of Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir, and Smotrich, an opposition government led by Eisenkot or someone else will lack the will or the political capacity to chart a radically different course.

“The way I see it, there will be a change, but not a dramatic one,” he said. “Eisenkot might 'protect democracy' and the courts in Israel, but when it comes to the Palestinians it won't change things much.”

The alarm is hardly confined to Palestinian activists. In June, dozens of former leaders of the Israeli establishment, including Prime Ministers, generals, a Nobel laureate, and heads of Mossad, sent Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir, Smotrich, and other ministers a letter protesting “Jewish terrorism” in the West Bank. They cited acts of murder, sexual violence, and desecration of the dead, carried out, they said, with “almost complete impunity.” Tamir Pardo, a former chief of Mossad, warned in the letter that the failure to halt such violence represented “an existential threat for the state of Israel and runs the risk of further slaughter in the manner of October 7th.” The signatories threatened legal action and wrote that the violence in the West Bank was “reminiscent of similar crimes and pogroms committed against our people by other nations in eastern Europe in the 19th and 20th centuries.”

Netanyahu did not respond. He generally reserves his Hebrew-language interviews for Channel 14 and speaks more freely to the foreign press. When he does address the crisis in the West Bank, he finds rhetorical means to diminish it. In a recent interview with CNN, he blamed the violence on a small group of young extremists, “a hundred and fifty or so what you would call juvenile delinquents” who were, he claimed, not themselves settlers.

Viewed from abroad, Netanyahu's grip on power can seem almost incomprehensible after years of scandal, brutality, and attacks on democratic institutions. Yet, despite his current peril in the polls, he may endure for a simple reason. He knows how to play on fear and has depicted himself as the only man ruthless enough to keep Israelis safe.

Nadav Eyal, the columnist for Yedioth Ahronoth , told me about meeting a woman recently in Kfar Aza, one of the kibbutzim hit hardest by Hamas. She was crying and said that she could no longer live near Palestinians. “If Netanyahu wins, it's because of that,” Eyal told me. “This is what people don't get. The sentiment in Israel, and Netanyahu understands it, is so powerfully about what has happened and how your worst fears were completely vindicated. From the outside, October 7th was another round of violence that ended with seventy thousand people dead. No, what happened on October 7th had never happened here before, a pogrom that triggered something here—the Jewish experience, over thousands of years. This is how Netanyahu gains power and maintains it. His skepticism, his distrust of the region around him, his devotion to the Iron Wall. His ability is to use the Israeli psyche. He represents a deep skepticism toward Arabs unless they accept Israel's dominance over the territory.”

Eyal was describing the emotional terrain on which Netanyahu hoped to survive. The response that Eisenkot's campaign had decided on was less a contrasting ideology than a contrasting character. In late June, Eisenkot formally launched Yashar's campaign at an event center in Hod HaSharon, north of Tel Aviv. It was a smoothly run, thoroughly scripted affair. During an outdoor reception before the rally, I spotted Nahum Barnea, the dean of Israeli journalism. He is eighty-one and slender as a stalk, and travels to his appointments by bicycle. He has been the acerbic bane of many Prime Ministers, including Netanyahu, yet he seemed encouraged by Eisenkot's candidacy, particularly by its projection of a sense of decency.

“He can stop the bleeding in two areas,” Barnea told me. The first was Israel's standing in the world. “Remember the old ad campaign for 7 UP? He is the 'un-cola.' ” The second was the country's polarization, the bitterness of its political discourse. Eisenkot might embody a different kind of public figure. “He's misleading because people see an overweight guy, like a bear, very warm and informal. He doesn't look like a general. But he is hardly mediocre. He is serious. And, yes, he lost his son in war. He knows that his bereavement is a political advantage, and not cynically. He represents a going back to public service.”

As “Golani Sheli,” the anthem of Eisenkot's old brigade, boomed from the speakers, the candidate walked onstage to loud applause. There was little ideology in his appeal, certainly nothing about a Palestinian state. The campaign had been built around service, sacrifice, reform, and repair. Whether those themes could compete with the fears Netanyahu had spent years cultivating was a question that the election would decide. ❖

雷诺阿女孩，凯瑟琳·奥斯特勒（Catherine Ostler）（Atria） 。这本关于法国犹太银行王朝的女儿们的全面传记——由雷诺阿绘制，普鲁斯特被视为家庭朋友——在两个平行的世界中展开：一个是光鲜亮丽的特权巴黎，另一个是普遍贫困和政治不稳定加剧了深刻的社会焦虑的巴黎。奥斯特勒在两个世界中追溯了反犹太仇恨的线索，她说明了姐妹俩的稀有生活如何经常受到突发偏见的损害。例如，1882 年，在完成女孩肖像后不久，雷诺阿就宣称他“正在向犹太人洗手”。正如奥斯特勒所表明的，他所说的理由含糊不清且无关紧要。雷诺阿只不过是反犹太主义的“潮流中的软木塞”。

《小蓝点》 ，凯瑟琳·邓恩 (Katherine Dunn)（布鲁姆斯伯里出版社）着。邓恩关于全球定位系统的引人入胜的历史始于第二次世界大战初期，当时德国人发现德国人正在使用无线电波轰炸看不见的目标。英国的反应——试图操纵德国的系统，同时开发自己的更复杂的系统——为技术军备竞赛奠定了基础，最终将产生 GPS 及其竞争对手。邓恩在数十年中跟踪这场比赛，探索了 GPS 背后的物理原理及其奇怪的二元性：如果这项技术现在几乎是平民生活中几乎看不见的特征，那么它仍然是一种“军事产品，旨在以惊人的精度投掷威力巨大的炸弹”。

我们正在读什么

发现著名的新小说、非小说和诗歌。

《空气》 ，作者：克里斯蒂安·克拉赫特 (Christian Kracht)，丹尼尔·鲍尔斯 (Daniel Bowles)（利夫赖特）从德文翻译而来。这部小说有两条故事线：一条以一位具有路德主义审美观的当代设计师为中心，另一条发生在一个奇幻的世界里，一个年轻女孩不小心射杀了一个她误以为是鹿的男人。在第一个情节中，设计师在挪威从事一个项目时在太阳风暴中失踪。在第二个故事中，女孩和男人逃离了恶毒统治者派来的士兵。在这个现实中，人们靠采集和捕杀的食物为生。他们穿着共用的衣服；他们没有镜子之类的发明，也没有——最重要的是——抗生素。尽管这个世界缺乏让设计师如此困扰的二十一世纪的装饰，但它的残酷也表明，对前现代的怀旧是一把双向的刀。

《我希望你幸福》 ，杰姆·考尔德（Jem Calder）（Farrar、Straus & Giroux）着。 “一个新的人发现你很有趣，会让你感觉焕然一新。”这本亲密小说的主角之一就是这样反映的，小说讲述了伦敦两位有志于创作的人之间的关系——一位是咖啡师，同时怀揣着诗歌梦想的年轻女子，另一位年纪稍大的男子是一名文案作家，但希望成为一名小说家。一天晚上，两人在酒吧见面，然后一起回家。当考尔德追踪他们的浪漫历程时，从早期小心翼翼的发短信到对人物阴暗元素的思考——文案作者、酗酒——他赋予了自我破坏和唯我论等人类常年特征的新面貌。
